summary: Hippalcimus (Ancient Greek: Ἱππάλκιμος; also Hippalcus, Hippalcmus) is, in this atlas entry, the son of Pelops and Hippodamia counted among the Argonauts from Pisa. A separate Boeotian Hippalcimus son of Itonus fathers the Trojan-War leader Peneleos.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ἱππάλκιμος; variants Hippalcus, Hippalcmus, Hippalmus appear in the lists.

sections.heading: Pelopid Argonaut
paragraphs: Hyginus (Fabulae 14) and related Argonaut catalogues include Hippalcimus or Hippalcus among the sons of Pelops and Hippodamia who sail with Jason from the Peloponnesian Pisa. He is a catalogue Argonaut without an independent episode in Apollonius.
The atlas character hippalcimus is typed to that Pelopid sailor — Pisa and the Argo — not to the Boeotian stem.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Diodorus and others know a Hippalcimus son of Itonus (son of Boeotus), father by Asterope of Peneleos, one of the Boeotian captains at Troy. Hippalmus pages collect further minor warriors and hunters. The atlas id hippalcimus must not be merged with those Boeotian or battlefield namesakes.
